Explain the Bag-of-Words model for image classification and contrast it with how CNNs represent images.
risposta: Bag-of-Words achieves spatial invariance by representing an image as a histogram of local features, ignoring their arrangement. Pipeline: detect/describe features (e.g. SIFT), cluster all training descriptors with k-means to form a visual vocabulary, assign each descriptor to its nearest visual word, represent each image by the frequency histogram of visual words, then train a classifier (e.g. SVM). CNNs instead learn hierarchical features end-to-end: convolutional layers apply learnable filters with weight sharing (far fewer parameters than fully-connected), pooling layers reduce resolution and grow the receptive field, and fully-connected layers classify; output uses softmax with cross-entropy loss. Transfer learning pre-trains on a large dataset then fine-tunes on a smaller task.

domanda: Describe the evolution of object detectors from R-CNN to Faster R-CNN and single-stage detectors.
risposta: Two-stage detectors propose regions then classify them. R-CNN (2014) used Selective Search for ~2k proposals and ran a CNN on each independently - accurate but slow. Fast R-CNN (2015) ran the CNN once on the whole image to make a feature map, projected proposals onto it, and used RoI Pooling to extract fixed-size features - much faster. Faster R-CNN (2015) replaced external proposals with a learnable Region Proposal Network that slides over the feature map and predicts objectness and box refinements relative to anchor boxes of various scales/aspect ratios. Single-stage detectors (YOLO, SSD) skip proposals and predict boxes and classes directly in one pass: faster but often less accurate. mAP (IoU >= 0.5) is the main metric.

domanda: Compare semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and panoptic segmentation, and explain the architectures involved.
risposta: Semantic segmentation labels every pixel with a class using an encoder-decoder: the encoder (e.g. ResNet) downsamples to learn high-level features, the decoder upsamples to a full-resolution map, and skip connections combine coarse decoder context with fine encoder detail (U-Net). Instance segmentation distinguishes individual object instances: Mask R-CNN extends Faster R-CNN with a parallel mask-prediction branch and replaces RoI Pooling with the more precise RoIAlign for accurate masks. Panoptic segmentation unifies the two, labeling amorphous stuff (sky, road) via semantic segmentation and countable things (cars, people) via instance segmentation into one comprehensive output. FPNs help by building a multi-scale feature pyramid with a top-down path and lateral connections.
